(ii) \(\mathrm{CH_3CN} \xrightarrow[\text{(b) } \mathrm{H_2O}]{\text{(a) DIBAL-H}}\)

questions._figure: ILLUSTRATIVE — In sub-item (iii) the reactant is printed as a DRAWN benzene ring (hexagon with alternating Kekule double bonds) bearing CONH2, not as a formula, over an arrow labelled H3O+ above and delta below. Sub-items (i) and (ii) are printed as ordinary formulas. The linear LaTeX in the stem is a faithful reading of that drawing and is corroborated by the marking scheme's answer (benzoic acid, so the ring is aromatic and the reactant is benzamide), but it is not what the page looks like, so the real crop should be attached. Page idx 4.

questions.stem:
Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their property as indicated :
(i) \(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\), \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}\), \(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_2CH_3}\), \(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\) (Reactivity towards HCN)
(ii) \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\), \(\mathrm{Cl-CH_2-COOH}\), \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH-COOH}\) (Acidic strength)
(iii) Benzoic acid, 4-Nitrobenzoic acid, 4-Methoxybenzoic acid (Acidic strength)
questions._figure: ILLUSTRATIVE — Two sub-items are printed as drawings. In (i) the third and fourth compounds are drawn two-dimensionally as CH3 - C - CH2 - CH3 and CH3 - C - CH3 with the carbonyl O on a vertical double bond below the central carbon; the stem reads them as the condensed formulas CH3COCH2CH3 and CH3COCH3, which is exactly how the marking scheme writes them. In (iii) all three compounds are DRAWN benzene rings each bearing COOH at the top vertex, the second carrying NO2 and the third OCH3 at the para (bottom) vertex, printed in that order; the stem names them, which is lossless here because the question asks for an ORDERING and naming a compound does not state that ordering. Both readings are corroborated by the marking scheme (CH3COCH2CH3 < CH3COCH3 < CH3CH2CHO < CH3CHO, and p-methoxybenzoic < benzoic < p-nitrobenzoic). Page idx 4.

questions.context: Amines constitute an important class of organic compounds derived by replacing one or more hydrogen atoms of ammonia molecule by alkyl/aryl groups. Amines are usually formed from nitro compounds, halides, amides, etc. They exhibit hydrogen bonding which influences their physical properties. Alkyl amines are found to be stronger bases than ammonia. In aromatic amines, electron releasing and withdrawing groups, respectively increase and decrease their basic character. Reactions of amines are governed by availability of the unshared pair of electrons on nitrogen. Influence of the number of hydrogen atoms at nitrogen atom on the type of reactions and nature of products is responsible for identification and distinction between primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Reactivity of aromatic amines can be controlled by acylation process.
